definitions.gloss: formation, origin, how something came to be
definitions.explanation: The process or history by which something was formed or established. Often used when explaining how a word, organization, or concept originated.
The way something is composed or made up of its constituent parts.

examples.japanese: この{漢字|かんじ}の{成|な}り{立|た}ちを{調|しら}べた。
examples.english: I looked up the origin of this kanji.

examples.japanese: {会社|かいしゃ}の{成|な}り{立|た}ちについて{説明|せつめい}してください。
examples.english: Please explain how the company was established.

examples.japanese: {日本語|にほんご}の{成|な}り{立|た}ちには、{中国語|ちゅうごくご}からの{影響|えいきょう}が{大|おお}きい。
examples.english: Chinese influence played a large role in the formation of the Japanese language.

examples.japanese: {社会|しゃかい}の{成|な}り{立|た}ちを{学|まな}ぶ。
examples.english: To study the makeup of society.

examples.japanese: {地球|ちきゅう}の{大気|たいき}の{成|な}り{立|た}ちは{複雑|ふくざつ}だ。
examples.english: The composition of Earth's atmosphere is complex.

examples.japanese: この{組織|そしき}の{成|な}り{立|た}ちを{理解|りかい}すれば、{問題|もんだい}の{原因|げんいん}が{見|み}えてくる。
examples.english: If you understand the structure of this organization, the cause of the problem becomes clear.

notes:
{成|な}り{立|た}ち is the noun form derived from the verb {成|な}り{立|た}つ (to be established, to consist of). It refers to either how something came into being or what something is made up of.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {漢字|かんじ}の{成|な}り{立|た}ち: origin of a kanji
- {言葉|ことば}の{成|な}り{立|た}ち: etymology of a word
- {社会|しゃかい}の{成|な}り{立|た}ち: makeup of society

RELATED WORDS:
- {成|な}り{立|た}つ: to be established, to consist of (verb)
- {由来|ゆらい}: origin, derivation
- {構成|こうせい}: composition, structure
